title: Prompt injection between agents
definition: One agent's output hijacks another's behaviour, directly or through a shared filesystem, clipboard or tool result.

title: Data leakage and scope violations
definition: One agent is authorised to see sensitive data and the other is not, and the second exposes what it should never have had.

title: Capability and permission conflicts
definition: Both agents hold authority over the same resource, and one's writes silently break the other's assumptions.

title: Cascading errors and hallucination amplification
definition: One agent confidently outputs something wrong and the other treats it as ground truth, compounding it across the boundary.
why_absent: Confirming this needs a criterion that can tell a compounded error from an ordinary one, which means a task with a checkable right answer and a second agent that acts on the first's output. None of the adversarial scenarios has that shape: they all plant something and watch for a side effect, and a wrong answer produces no side effect to watch.

title: Compliance and policy violations from composition
definition: Each agent complies on its own, and the combination produces a workflow that does not.
why_absent: Confirming this needs a policy to violate, and a policy is a fact about an organisation rather than about a pair of agents. Nothing in a sandbox on one machine can establish it without the harness inventing the rule it then finds broken, which would be measuring this project's imagination.
